# Third-party components: reqlint

These are **not** part of the CC0 1.0 dedication of this tool. Each keeps its own licence; none is copied into this folder unless the row says so. Licences were identified on 20 Oct 2026 from the projects' own metadata; re-check before a release ([check] where marked).

| Component | Used for | Licence | Distributed here? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Python 3.10+ standard library | everything (reqlint has no runtime dependencies) | PSF License | No (installed by the user) |
| setuptools | packaging (build only) | MIT | No |
| pytest | tests only | MIT | No |

**Third-party text.** The rule set is the course's own, *inspired by* the requirement-quality characteristics in the INCOSE *Guide to Writing Requirements* (GtWR). No GtWR text, rule wording or examples are reproduced; messages and explanations are paraphrase written for SYS 5100. "INCOSE" is a trademark of the International Council on Systems Engineering and is used only to cite the Guide. EARS (Mavin et al. 2009) is cited by name; its pattern names are used with attribution.

**Copied code.** None. All source files were written for this course (by Claude agents under the instructor's direction; see `docs/AI_DISCLOSURE.md`).
